data.narrative:
Gravitics is a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by Colin Doughan that has raised $20M in equity plus $60M in STRATFI funding. The sector encompasses 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Only one valuation method is reliably applicable given available data. Stage-progression analysis uses the $20M raised as a value proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $50M. Peer-median analysis is not feasible: while 11 same-sector private peers exist, none meets minimum thresholds (need ≥3) when filtered by stage or valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because the target's revenue is not disclosed, preventing calculation of meaningful price-to-sales multiples despite the sector median of 23.9x across public comps.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with a median of $50M. This range reflects meaningful uncertainty: the analysis rests on a single method without triangulation support. Key unknowns include Gravitics' current revenue run-rate or path to profitability, which would enable public-comp anchoring, and the absence of sufficiently detailed private peer financials to support peer-median benchmarking. The STRATFI component ($60M) should be evaluated separately to clarify its instrument type and impact on equity value.
